citely.title: when the paper makes a claim but the source trail is missing
citely.caption: When a paper makes a claim but the source trail is messy, I check where the evidence actually comes from first.
citely.pinned: Would you check the claim first or the reference list first?

citely.title: me checking references before trusting them
citely.caption: References can look real and still be off. I would verify the details before I build my paper around them.
citely.pinned: The scary part is when a citation looks real at first glance.

citely.title: AI references can look way too real
citely.caption: AI references can look convincing. I use Citely to check the source trail before relying on one.
citely.pinned: This is your sign to check AI references before trusting them.

figpad.title: when the paper needs a figure but my sketch is a mess
figpad.caption: When the paper needs a figure, I would rather generate a draft I can still edit than use a flat image.
figpad.pinned: Editable figure draft > flat image you cannot fix.

figpad.title: when the only figure file I have is a flat image
figpad.caption: Flat figure assets are painful to edit. FigPad SVG Converter helps turn an image into an editable SVG workflow.
figpad.pinned: This is for turning a figure image into something easier to keep editing.

figpad.title: when the paper figure also has to go into slides
figpad.caption: If the figure has to move into slides later, editable PPT export is the workflow I would want.
figpad.pinned: For anyone who has had to rebuild a figure inside slides.

clearfy.title: when my paper draft sounds too AI-clean
clearfy.caption: Before submitting, I would check which sentences sound too AI-heavy instead of guessing.
clearfy.pinned: The highlighted sentences are the part I would review first.

clearfy.title: when the paragraph is technically correct but sounds robotic
clearfy.caption: When a paragraph sounds stiff, I use Clearfy to help revise the wording and then still read it myself.
clearfy.pinned: I would still edit the final version myself, but this helps with the stiff parts.

clearfy.title: the check first then fix workflow
clearfy.caption: Check what sounds AI-heavy first, then revise the stiff sentences. That workflow makes more sense than editing blind.
clearfy.pinned: Check first, then fix. Much less guessing.
